subject: Slice 5 mark fixup requested by the coordinator on size: tuple field marks move from three empty spans per tuple to generated attribute-keyed pseudo-element CSS plus one bare <i> per tuple. Supersedes nothing in the slice-5 evidence record, which stays valid for 46918be.
authority: .syzygy/governance/decisions/POLARIS-PURSUIT-OWNER-RULINGS-P68-P83-DECISION.md P-70 under .syzygy/governance/decisions/PWB-IMPLEMENTATION-AUTHORIZATION-CONTINUATION-ACT.md. No PocModel, machine, schema, route, read, egress or governed change.

design.marks: Generated from TIER_ENCODING, TIER_ABSENCE_ENCODING, FRESHNESS_ENCODING and CHALLENGE_ENCODING (TUPLE_MARKS_CSS): .claim-tuple[data-epistemic-tier=v]::after, .claim-tuple[data-epistemic-freshness=v] + i::before, .claim-tuple[data-challenge-state=v] + i::after, each { content: " " / ""; color: var(); }. The tuple stays one text node; the only markup is one bare after it.
design.whyNotZeroDom: The tuple's ::before already carries the M3.1 label symbol, so one pseudo-element (::after) is free, and it takes one colour. The declaration gives fields different tokens on served tuples (live: 13 tuples pair ∅ --muted with ◌ --ink; stale/broken/superseded --muted beside unchallenged --ink), so a single ::after would either change the reviewed token table or ignore the token for two fields. One bare <i> supplies two more pseudo-elements at 7 B.
design.accessibility: Every mark symbol keeps empty alternative text (content: "x " / ""); the tuple words carry every value. Mutant S5-F5 (alt text dropped) is killed.
design.glossary: Unchanged: the glossary rows keep the .tt-<value> classes and TUPLE_FIELD_TREATMENTS_CSS.

measurement.method: measure.sh: clean detached checkout of 30d685c1 in the dov.3.2 worktree, npm run build:poc, private daemon --port 0 --state-dir <scratch>, GET /, /polaris, /trajectory, /orrery direct and with Host: tzeusy.parrot-hen.ts.net. Base (37c5da93) and slice 5 (46918be) are the captures recorded in the predecessor record, same Butlers commit.

census.method: Two methods per page and form: the test's serverCensus (body without style/script, every tuple followed by , each value's served rule present) and its browser TreeWalker census (selector count vs walked, computed content and colour of each field's pseudo-element), over the eight captured files.
